items.answer: An intranet is a private network for an organisation's members only; the internet is the public, global network of networks.

items.stem: Give one argument for and one argument against this view: "All employees should work through a VPN when outside the office."

items.stem: Distinguish between a router and a switch.

items.stem: A switch has an empty MAC address table. Hosts are connected as follows: E on port 1, D on port 2, B on port 3, A on port 4. These frames are sent in order: B to D, A to D, B to E. For each frame state whether the switch floods it or forwards it to a single port, and give the final MAC table.
items.answer: B→D: flooded to all ports except 3; A→D: flooded to all ports except 4; B→E: flooded to all ports except 3. Final table: A: port 4, B: port 3
items.markingKey: The switch records the source MAC/port of every frame; unknown destinations are flooded. B→D: flooded to all ports except 3; A→D: flooded to all ports except 4; B→E: flooded to all ports except 3. Final table A: port 4, B: port 3. 1 mark per frame, 1 for the table.

items.stem: Briefly explain why a switch reduces network congestion compared with a hub.
items.answer: The switch learns which MAC address is on each port and forwards each frame only to the destination port, so other links are not filled with traffic and several pairs can communicate at once; a hub broadcasts every frame to every port.

items.stem: A factory has 4 production halls, each with 20 machines. Compare a star in each hall connected by a bus backbone with a star in each hall connected by a mesh of core switches, calculating the number of backbone links for the mesh and discussing reliability, cost and performance.
items.answer: Mesh of 4 core switches = 4×3/2 = 6 links vs 3 segments on the bus. Mesh: any single backbone failure is bypassed, higher aggregate bandwidth, but more cost and configuration. Bus: cheap but a single break splits halls and the backbone is a bottleneck. Hybrid star-mesh recommended for a factory where downtime is costly.

items.stem: Briefly explain why network segmentation improves security.

Supported judgement: A star (or extended star with a small redundant core) is more appropriate for a school; mesh suits critical backbones. Case study context: Lumen Library, a city library service in Lisbon, offers public Wi-Fi, an online catalogue and e-book lending, and runs its servers in a small on-site data room.
(a) "Devices in different VLANs on the same switch can always talk directly." Explain the flaw in this statement. Refer to Lumen Library in your answer. [2]
(b) "Every organisation should segment its network into many small subnets." To what extent do you agree with this statement? Refer to Lumen Library in your answer. [4]
items.answer: (a) VLANs are separate broadcast domains; traffic between them must pass through a router or layer-3 switch. (b) Segmentation by function and security level is good practice; the number of segments should match the organisation's size and risk.

Arguments against: more complex to configure and troubleshoot; needs routing between segments, adding cost; too many subnets can waste addresses.
